name: aggindex-minmax-allnull-group-dropped
tables: CREATE TABLE t (id BIGINT NOT NULL, g BIGINT, v BIGINT, PRIMARY KEY (id))
CREATE INDEX max_by_g AS SELECT MAX(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
CREATE INDEX min_by_g AS SELECT MIN(v) FROM t GROUP BY g

groups.name: max-allnull-group-dropped_BUG
groups.reason: ENGINE BUG: GROUP BY g over the table yields a group for every distinct g present; g=2 has two rows (all v NULL) so MAX(v)=NULL and [2, NULL] MUST appear. `WHERE id IS NOT NULL` is always true (id is a NOT NULL PK) so it selects the identical rows and must yield the identical grouped result. It does not: the index-backed MAX (q0) omits the all-NULL group g=2 entirely, while the scan-backed MAX (q1) correctly returns [2, NULL]. The max_ever_long aggregate index writes no entry for a group whose aggregate is NULL, so a GROUP BY served by that index loses the whole group.
queries: SELECT g, MAX(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
SELECT g, MAX(v) FROM t WHERE id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY g

groups.name: min-allnull-group-dropped_BUG
groups.reason: ENGINE BUG: same defect for the MIN aggregate index. g=2 (all v NULL) must appear as [2, NULL]; the index-backed MIN (q0) drops it, the scan-backed MIN (q1) returns it.
queries: SELECT g, MIN(v) FROM t GROUP BY g
SELECT g, MIN(v) FROM t WHERE id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY g
